name: AdaBoost
tagline: Adaptive boosting: classification reweights samples by exponential loss, regression uses AdaBoost.R2 with normalized linear loss.
formula: $$\text{cls: } \alpha_m = \eta\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\log\!\frac{1-\epsilon_m}{\epsilon_m},\;\; w_i \leftarrow w_i\,e^{\alpha_m\,\mathbb{1}[h_m(x_i)\neq y_i]}; \qquad \text{reg: } e_i = |h_m(x_i)-r_i|/\max_j|\cdot|,\; \beta = \bar{e}/(1-\bar{e}),\; w_i \leftarrow w_i\,\beta^{1-e_i}$$
diff_from_baseline: Freund & Schapire, 'A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning and an Application to Boosting' (JCSS 1997); regression is Drucker, 'Improving Regressors using Boosting Techniques' (1997, AdaBoost.R2). Original adaptive boosting; reweights samples toward errors.

name: Gradient Boosting
tagline: Friedman gradient boosting: each round fits a weak learner to the negative gradient of the loss (residuals for SE, $y - \sigma(F)$ for log-loss).
diff_from_baseline: Friedman, 'Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine' (Annals of Statistics 2001). Sample weights stay uniform; the boosting signal comes from fitting weak learners to pseudo-residuals. Newton line search for classification step size.

name: XGBoost-style (Newton)
tagline: Second-order boosting: leaf weights $\alpha_m$ from Newton step using gradient $g$ and Hessian $h$, with L2 regularization $\lambda$.
diff_from_baseline: Chen & Guestrin, 'XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System' (KDD 2016). Newton-style weighted leaf updates with L2 regularization; the foundation of modern gradient boosting libraries (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost).
